overview: Liz Ammons and John Anderson of the Medford Historical Society and Museum discussed the organization's mission to preserve the city's diverse history through exhibits and community outreach. They highlighted the society's extensive digitized Civil War photograph collection and current exhibits focused on migration and American independence.

items.title: Introduction and Museum Basics
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced museum volunteers Liz Ammons and John Anderson to discuss the facility's operations at 10 Governors Avenue and its Sunday public hours.

items.title: Mission and Membership Details
items.summary: Ammons outlined the society's mission to foster an inclusive understanding of Medford’s history and diversity through programs and museum displays; membership is open to the public starting at $25.

items.title: History of the Historical Society
items.summary: Anderson detailed the history of the society since its 1896 founding and the construction of its purpose-built headquarters in 1916 by developer Moses Mann.

items.title: Museum Exhibits on Migration and Independence
items.summary: Ammons described the traveling 'Migration' exhibit and the current '1776 and Beyond' display, which links the Declaration of Independence to local justice movements like abolition and suffrage.

items.title: Civil War Photograph Collection
items.summary: Anderson explained the origins of the society's significant Civil War photograph collection, which was donated by the Grand Army of the Republic and is now digitized for public access.

items.title: Community Outreach and Education
items.summary: The guests discussed community engagement efforts including high school internships, elementary school field trips, and free public lectures hosted at the Medford Public Library.

items.title: Local Landmarks and Research Resources
items.summary: The group discussed historical South Medford landmarks, such as former horse racing tracks, and the research space available for public inquiries.
